summary.en: DWD (Disability and Working Development) strengthens disability-inclusive education and supports children with disabilities to access and thrive in mainstream classrooms.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Ensure children who are deaf or hard of hearing, and children with other disabilities, can access, participate in and complete quality education alongside their peers.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Sign-language coaching cycles are running in all partner schools this school year, with monthly follow-up visits from KAPE inclusive-education officers.
Screening camps completed in the latest quarter referred a new cohort of children for hearing and vision services, with assistive devices distributed at school level.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Train teachers in Cambodian Sign Language and inclusive classroom practice
Provide assistive devices, learning aids and accessible materials
Support screening, referral and follow-up with health services
Work with families and communities to reduce stigma and increase enrolment
Adapt school infrastructure for physical accessibility

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Children who are deaf or hard of hearing in mainstream primary and secondary schools
Children with physical, visual and intellectual disabilities
Teachers, school directors and school support committees
Parents and caregivers of children with disabilities

blocks.heading: Impact
items: More children with disabilities enrolled and retained in mainstream classrooms
Teachers confident using sign language and adapted materials in daily lessons
Reduced stigma reported by families and community members
Accessible school facilities that keep children in school year after year

items.title: A signing classroom
items.text: A rural primary school introduced daily sign-language practice for all pupils, so deaf classmates are included in play as well as lessons.

items.title: Back to school
items.text: A boy with a mobility impairment returned to Grade 4 after a ramp and accessible latrine were built with community contributions.

summary.en: AIR (AI Readiness) prepares Cambodian schools, teachers and students for the responsible integration of artificial intelligence in learning.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Prepare Cambodian schools, teachers and learners to use artificial intelligence safely, ethically and productively, so that AI strengthens rather than replaces good teaching.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: AI literacy modules are being piloted with teachers and students in partner schools, alongside a growing library of Khmer-language resources.
Teacher coaching sessions on responsible use of AI tools run every month in target provinces.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Develop an AI-readiness curriculum and Khmer-language teaching resources for lower and upper secondary schools
Train teachers and school leaders on AI literacy, prompt design and academic-integrity policy
Establish student AI clubs that build small, locally-relevant AI projects
Run community awareness sessions on responsible AI use, privacy and misinformation
Produce an AI readiness assessment used to guide school improvement planning

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Secondary school students
Teachers and ICT focal points
School directors and provincial education officers

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Students able to use AI tools critically, safely and productively
Teachers integrating AI-supported activities into lesson plans
A growing base of Khmer-language AI learning materials

items.title: An AI club that answers local questions
items.text: Grade 11 students trained a simple classifier to sort community questions to the right commune office, presenting their model at the district science fair.

items.title: Teachers redesign assessment
items.text: After AI-literacy training, a school team replaced take-home essays with in-class oral defences, keeping assessment fair in the age of generative tools.

summary.en: IDEAL (Integrated Digital Education for Adolescent Learners) blends classroom and online learning for lower-secondary students.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Improve digital education for all learners by embedding digital tools, media literacy and project-based learning in everyday classroom practice.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Digital learning labs are active in partner schools, with student exhibitions held annually to showcase learning outcomes.
Recent exhibitions at Chaktomuk Secondary School and Hun Neang Bak Kheng Primary School demonstrated student projects to parents and officials.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Establish and mentor school study clubs across core subjects
Equip schools with digital corners, tablets and shared learning resources
Coach teachers on project-based learning and digital lesson design
Organise annual student achievement exhibitions to showcase learning
Support school management committees to plan and sustain digital education

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Primary and secondary students in target schools
Teachers delivering ICT and digital learning
School management and parent communities

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Thousands of students gaining hands-on digital skills each year
Teachers confidently running digital and blended lessons
Schools with sustainable ICT labs and maintenance plans

items.title: Bak Kheng Primary School
items.text: Students designed and presented their own booths on coding, science and Khmer arts at the annual exhibition, explaining their own thinking rather than reciting lessons.

items.title: Chaktomuk Secondary School
items.text: Seventeen study clubs, from Earth Science to Mathematics, turned a year of research into a school-wide exhibition attended by around 350 people.

summary.en: Lotus Outreach partners with KAPE to keep marginalised girls and at-risk children — particularly in rural communities — enrolled and learning.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Reduce dropout and trafficking risk for the most vulnerable girls by combining scholarships, safe transport, counselling and community engagement.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Scholarship disbursements and mentoring visits are on schedule for the current academic year.
Life-skills and safeguarding sessions have been delivered to all scholarship recipients and their families.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Provide scholarships, bicycles and school materials to at-risk girls
Deliver counselling and protection case management
Run community awareness on child protection and safe migration
Support school-based girls' clubs and peer networks
Coordinate referrals with local authorities and social services

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Girls at high risk of dropping out, trafficking or early marriage
Poor rural families with school-aged daughters
Lower- and upper-secondary students needing financial support

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Scholarship girls progressing to upper secondary and higher education
Families better informed on safe migration and child protection
Reduced dropout among the most vulnerable girls in target schools

items.title: A bicycle changes attendance
items.text: Girls living more than five kilometres from school raised their attendance sharply after receiving bicycles and a safe-route plan.

items.title: Girls' club leadership
items.text: A school girls' club led a campaign on reporting harassment, supported by trained teacher counsellors.

summary.en: CTSP (Children Targeted Support Program) provides individualised support for children with disabilities, including assistive devices and specialist teachers.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Keep vulnerable girls and at-risk children in school through targeted scholarships, mentoring and family support.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Community teaching and support activities continue across partner communes, with tutoring groups meeting weekly outside regular class hours.
Case management records are reviewed each quarter so that children at risk of dropping out receive timely follow-up.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Award scholarships covering school materials, transport and living support
Provide case management and mentoring for each scholar
Run life-skills and study-skills sessions for scholarship recipients
Engage parents and guardians to protect school attendance
Track retention, transition and completion for every scholar

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Out-of-school and at-risk children
Children from poor and migrant families
Community volunteers and local teachers
Commune councils and school support committees

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Higher re-enrolment and retention among children previously out of school
Stronger community structures supporting vulnerable learners
Improved literacy and numeracy for children in catch-up classes

items.title: Staying in Grade 9
items.text: A scholarship and monthly mentoring kept a student in school after her family's harvest failed.

items.title: First in the family
items.text: A CTSP scholar became the first person in her family to sit the Grade 12 national exam.

summary.en: MIDL (Media and Information Digital Literacy) equips youth with critical thinking, online safety, and digital citizenship skills.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Build media and information digital literacy so young Cambodians can evaluate online information, protect themselves online and participate as responsible digital citizens.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Media and information literacy curricula are being rolled out in partner schools and youth clubs.
Youth-led campaigns against misinformation are running on social media with KAPE mentoring.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Deliver MIDL curriculum sessions in secondary schools and youth centres
Train teacher-facilitators and youth peer educators
Run campus and online campaigns against misinformation and online harm
Produce Khmer-language media-literacy videos and printed toolkits
Support youth-led community research on local information needs

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Secondary students and youth club members
Teachers and youth facilitators
Parents and wider community audiences

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Young people better able to identify misinformation online
Active youth clubs producing their own digital content
Teachers equipped with ready-to-use MIL lesson plans

items.title: Fact-checking the feed
items.text: A youth team traced a viral health rumour to its source and produced a Khmer explainer video that reached tens of thousands of local viewers.

items.title: Safer classrooms online
items.text: Peer educators supported classmates facing online harassment and helped their school adopt a clear reporting procedure.

summary.en: CamScam supports STEM, computing and maker-space initiatives in Cambodian secondary schools.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Protect Cambodian internet users, especially students and young workers, from online scams and digital financial fraud through awareness, skills and community reporting.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Awareness sessions on online scams and digital fraud are being delivered in schools and communities.
Reporting and referral guidance has been shared with school directors and local authorities.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Develop anti-scam awareness materials in Khmer for schools and communities
Train students, teachers and parents to recognise and report common scams
Partner with local authorities on referral and reporting pathways
Run school and social-media anti-scam campaigns
Collect and publish anonymised case data to inform prevention

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Students and youth using social media
Parents, teachers and school staff
Community members vulnerable to online fraud

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Increased reporting and avoidance of online scams in target areas
Schools able to run their own awareness sessions
Safer online behaviour among young internet users

items.title: A scam stopped in the classroom
items.text: After a session on job-offer scams, a Grade 12 student recognised a fraudulent recruitment message and warned her whole class.

items.title: Community reporting desk
items.text: A commune-level reporting desk piloted with local authorities handled dozens of cases in its first six months.

summary.en: Digital and Virtual Teaching for Sciences & Arts (DViTSA), a sub-project of KAPE's Digital Education Program.

blocks.heading: Project goal
items: Strengthen digital and vocational skills for in-school and out-of-school adolescents, opening pathways to further study and decent work.

blocks.heading: Project update
items: Digital vocational and technical skills training cohorts are running with partner institutions.
Employer linkages and internship placements are being expanded for graduating trainees.

blocks.heading: Key activities
items: Deliver digital and vocational skills modules in partner schools and centres
Link learners with local employers for internships and job shadowing
Train instructors on competency-based, hands-on teaching
Provide career guidance and portfolio-building support
Support small start-up grants for youth enterprise ideas

blocks.heading: Target group
items: Out-of-school youth and TVET students
Young women seeking digital career pathways
Training institutions and employers

blocks.heading: Impact
items: Trainees placed in digital and technology-related jobs
Stronger institutional capacity to deliver digital skills courses
Increased participation of young women in technology careers

items.title: From club to contract
items.text: Two graduates of the digital design module now work part-time for a local printing business while continuing their studies.

items.title: Second chance learners
items.text: Out-of-school youth completed a basic ICT and life-skills course and re-entered formal education through the equivalency programme.
